data.summary: companions reports a companion 'installed but no agent is configured to launch it' when .mcp.json launches it under a different server key: run_nemo_run's .mcp.json has 'coding-guides' running docker.io/delian/codeguide-mcp, yet adopt and 'ddflow companions' say codeguide is not wired up and advise 'companions add --id codeguide', which would register it a second time. Detection matches the server key name, not the launch command/image.

hooks install, refusing over an existing pre-commit hook, tells the operator to add the check-commit line to .git/hooks/pre-commit even when that file carries 'File generated by pre-commit' (run_nemo_run): pre-commit regenerates it on install, so the edit is silently lost. It should detect the pre-commit framework header and advise a local hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml instead (relates to B-precommit-integration).

adopt run from inside a linked worktree writes the project's TRACKED files into the PRIMARY checkout (repo_root resolves via --git-common-dir): on run_nemo_run it appended to the primary's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, edited .mcp.json and .gitattributes and created docs/ddflow/, leaving the shared primary dirty while the caller's worktree got nothing. The shared event log belongs in the primary; files meant to be committed through the caller's branch belong in the caller's own tree (--show-toplevel). It also then 'kept' .claude/commands/implement.md because it looked at the primary's copy, not the worktree where it had been deleted.
